title: Pre-Progenitor Structure Modulation and 3D Hydrodynamic Fluctuations in Pulsar Birth: A Joint Statistical Framework
question: How are pulsars formed? Specifically, to what extent are neutron star birth properties (mass, spin, magnetic field, space velocity) systematically determined by progenitor structure (core compactness and envelope mass) versus stochastically dispersed by 3D hydrodynamic instabilities (SASI, convection) during core collapse?
hypothesis: Pulsar birth properties (mass, spin, magnetic field) are subject to systematic modulation by progenitor structure (envelope mass and core compactness), but hydrodynamic instabilities (SASI, convection) in 3D collapse introduce non-negligible stochastic dispersion. Specifically, the progenitor's core compactness (xi parameter) systematically influences nascent neutron star gravitational mass, while envelope mass indirectly modulates final mass and spin through explosion energy and fallback accretion. This relationship must be jointly tested by combining progenitor spectroscopic observations, supernova explosion energy measurements, and population statistics of pulsar birth properties.
background: Pulsar formation via core-collapse supernovae remains incompletely understood. The standard picture (F1: astro-ph/0103015) holds that pulsars (neutron stars) form from the collapse of massive stars, with neutrino energy deposition driving the explosion. However, the birth properties of neutron stars — mass, spin, magnetic field, and space velocity — are poorly constrained observationally (F2: astro-ph/0402200). Recent advances in 3D core-collapse supernova modeling (F3: 2604.24970) have demonstrated significant predictive power, while global comparisons (F4: 1806.04175) show that different simulation codes produce comparable results when initial conditions are controlled, yet residual differences remain. Core-collapse supernovae exhibit regularity within diversity (F10: astro-ph/0301006), with envelope mass being one of the driving parameters. The relative contributions of systematic progenitor structure modulation versus stochastic 3D hydrodynamic fluctuations to pulsar birth properties have not been quantitatively separated. Previous mechanisms such as magnetic field-driven kicks (F5: astro-ph/9707120) and neutrino oscillation-induced anisotropy (F6: astro-ph/0206471) operate in limited parameter spaces and produce effects too small to explain observed pulsar velocities alone.
rationale: This plan addresses all six required changes from the critique: (1) H1 magnetic field-kick positive correlation is completely abandoned — this direction has been thoroughly explored by Kisslinger (2006, hep-ph/0612221) and Lambiase & Poddar (2024, 2412.08446), offering no novelty. Instead, magnetic field is treated as one of the birth properties modulated by progenitor structure, not as an independent kick mechanism. (2) H2 derivation chain is corrected: (a) F10's 'envelope mass as one driving parameter' is NOT extrapolated to 'primary determinant' — it is retained as a secondary modulator through fallback; (b) F2's observational insufficiency is NOT used to support a positive assertion — it is used only to identify the knowledge gap; (c) 3D simulation stochastic fluctuations (F3, F4) are explicitly acknowledged as contributing non-negligible dispersion, forming a dual-factor framework with systematic modulation. (3) H3 independent channel is completely abandoned — millisecond pulsar formation via binary accretion (recycling) is textbook knowledge since the 1980s (Alpar et al. 1982, Smarr & Blandford 1977), and F7 merely quantifies minimum accretion rate within the recycling framework. F8 (2604.06472) confirms no evidence for a distinct white dwarf channel. (4) Novelty is explicitly contrasted with arXiv prior art:区别于 F1 的综述框架、F5/F6 的纯磁场/中微子不对称机制、F4 的代码比对工作，本研究的新颖性在于提出前身星结构参数(compactness+包层质量)与3D随机涨落的联合调制模型，定量分离系统性与随机成分。 (5) Applicability of deductive premises is checked: F5's mirror symmetry breaking depends on specific neutrino oscillation parameter space (extreme magnetic fields only); F6 acknowledges small effect magnitude at lowest order; F10's 'one of' qualifier is preserved throughout. (6) Data feasibility is explicitly addressed: progenitor envelope mass can only be independently measured for a handful of supernovae (e.g., SN 1987A, SN 2004et via pre-explosion imaging); pulsar 3D velocities require distance + proper motion + radial velocity (radial velocity unavailable for most pulsars). We address this via Bayesian hierarchical modeling with partial pooling, leveraging population statistics rather than requiring complete individual measurements.
approach: The research employs a four-phase approach: Phase 1 — Construct a grid of progenitor models using MESA stellar evolution code spanning ZAMS masses 8-25 solar masses and metallicities Z=0.001-0.02, extracting pre-collapse core compactness (xi_2.5 = M(r<2500km)/M_sun) and envelope mass for each model. Phase 2 — Select representative progenitor models and simulate 3D radiation-hydrodynamic core collapse using FLASH/CASTRO, capturing neutrino-driven convection and SASI instabilities, running to 1 second post-bounce, recording neutron star gravitational mass, initial spin period, and kick velocity vector. Phase 3 — For each (compactness, M_env) combination, perform >=10 simulations with different random seeds to quantify hydrodynamic fluctuation-induced property dispersion. Phase 4 — Build a Bayesian hierarchical model: systematic component f_sys(M_NS, P_0, v_kick | xi_2.5, M_env) + stochastic component epsilon ~ N(0, sigma_stoch), where sigma_stoch is calibrated from multi-code comparisons (F4: 1806.04175). Use PyMC3 MCMC sampling to fit observational data (ATNF pulsar catalog + Gaia DR3 proper motions + supernovae with known progenitors). Validate via leave-one-out cross-validation and posterior predictive checks. Compare against purely systematic model (no random term) and purely stochastic model (no progenitor dependence) using Bayes factors.

baselines: Purely stochastic model (no progenitor dependence) — tests whether 3D fluctuations alone can explain birth property distributions
Deterministic mapping only (no 3D fluctuation term) — tests whether progenitor structure alone suffices
Magnetic field-driven kick model (astro-ph/9707120 baseline) — tests the abandoned H1 direction against our dual-factor model
Neutrino oscillation kick model (astro-ph/0206471 baseline) — tests an alternative kick mechanism
Standard population synthesis (e.g., Cosmic-Ray code) — tests against conventional approaches without explicit progenitor structure
metrics: Bayesian evidence (log marginal likelihood) for model comparison between dual-factor and single-component models
Posterior predictive p-value for goodness-of-fit against observed pulsar birth property distributions
Root mean square error on natal mass prediction compared to observed neutron star mass distribution
Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic on predicted vs observed kick velocity distribution
Coverage probability of 95% credible intervals for birth property predictions
Variance decomposition ratio: fraction of total variance explained by systematic progenitor modulation vs stochastic 3D fluctuations

expectedOutcomes: We predict that: (1) core compactness xi_2.5 systematically correlates with neutron star gravitational mass, with Delta M_grav ~ 0.3 M_sun across the xi_2.5 range 0.1-0.5, exceeding the observed mass distribution standard deviation (~0.15 M_sun) and thus statistically detectable; (2) envelope mass M_env > 5 M_sun modulates fallback accretion (~0.1 M_sun) and angular momentum transfer, producing initial spin periods P ~ 10-50 ms consistent with young pulsar observations; (3) 3D stochastic fluctuations from SASI and convection contribute sigma_v ~ 50-100 km/s to kick velocity dispersion, consistent with observed proper motion scatter; (4) the dual-factor model achieves posterior predictive checks with p-values > 0.1 against current pulsar population data; (5) systematic progenitor modulation explains >30% of variance in at least one birth property (most likely mass), with the remainder attributed to stochastic 3D effects. These outcomes will provide the first quantitative separation of deterministic and stochastic contributions to pulsar birth properties.
risks: Key risks and mitigations: (1) Computational cost — each 3D simulation requires ~10^6 CPU-hours; 20 progenitors x 10 seeds = 200 simulations totaling ~2x10^8 CPU-hours. Mitigation: use adaptive mesh refinement and leverage national supercomputing facilities with ~10^4 core parallelism, completing in ~1 month. (2) Data scarcity — only ~15 supernovae have progenitor constraints, and only ~200 pulsars have reliable 3D velocities. Mitigation: Bayesian hierarchical model with partial pooling allows borrowing strength across the population; Gaia DR3 and future SKA data will expand samples. (3) Model misspecification — the assumed functional form f_sys may not capture true progenitor-property relationships. Mitigation: use Gaussian process regression for flexible non-parametric mapping, and validate with posterior predictive checks. (4) Systematic uncertainties in observations — pulsar magnetic fields inferred from spin-down have dipole decay uncertainty; distances affect velocity estimates. Mitigation: include observation error models as hyperparameters in the hierarchical framework. (5) Code dependence — different 3D codes may give different fluctuation magnitudes. Mitigation: use results from F4 (1806.04175) global comparison to calibrate stochastic term, and perform sensitivity analysis across codes.
